obs.subtitle: Add the overlays to OBS in a few steps.
obs.step1.title: Keep the companion running
obs.step1.body: Start qsc (run qsc --open to also open this dashboard) and leave it running while you stream. It can also start automatically with your computer: see the Run at startup section of the README.
obs.step2.title: Add a Browser source
obs.step2.body: In OBS, click the plus under Sources, then choose Browser.
obs.step3.title: Paste the overlay link
obs.step3.body: Copy the link from the Overlays page, where you can also choose a look, and paste it in the URL field of the Browser source.
obs.step4.title: Set the width and height
obs.step4.body: Use the recommended size of each overlay so nothing is clipped. The links below have no options; the Overlays page builds links with your look.
obs.step5.title: Recommended settings
obs.step5.item2: Leave Shutdown source when not visible unchecked, so the overlay stays in sync with the game.
obs.step5.item3: Refresh browser when scene becomes active is optional.
obs.step5.item4: No custom CSS is needed. Leave the field as OBS filled it in.
obs.step6.title: Position and layer the sources
obs.step6.body: Add one Browser source per overlay and arrange them in your scene. For example: the result card next to the game capture, the history below it, and the state badge in a corner.
obs.step7.title: Troubleshooting
obs.trouble1.title: Nothing shows
obs.trouble1.body: Run the connection check below and look at the Status page. The port in the link must match the one in Settings, and the host must be 127.0.0.1 or localhost.
obs.trouble2.title: The old style stays after editing a custom theme
obs.trouble2.body: Right-click the source in OBS and choose Refresh cache of current page.
obs.trouble3.title: The Pixel shadow looks blurry or clipped
obs.trouble3.body: Make the browser source larger than the recommended size, so the shadow has room.
obs.trouble4.title: OBS runs on another PC
obs.trouble4.body: The companion only answers on 127.0.0.1, so run OBS on the same machine. With a port forward, the Host of the link must match what the companion accepts.
obs.check_bad: Some checks failed. Open the Status page for details.
obs.custom.title: Create your own
obs.custom.body: Build an overlay of your own with plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript. The guide lists the data the companion publishes and gives two complete examples.

overlays.keys.name: Lane keys
overlays.keys.description: Lane bars that light up while a key is held, press counters and keys per second. Needs lane keys turned on in Settings. Use 480 x 200 for 4K and 560 x 200 for 7K.
overlays.curve.name: Judgment curve
overlays.curve.description: Draws the accuracy of the last play judgment by judgment, with a tick for each miss. It appears when a play is saved. Use 520 x 180.
overlays.counts_hint: Shows the number of presses under each lane. On by default.
overlays.peak_hint: Shows the highest keys per second of the map. On by default.
settings.keys.title: Lane keys
settings.keys.disclosure: Off by default. When on, only the lane keys you choose below are read, and only while a map is being played. Nothing is stored or logged. The key state is read system wide, regardless of the focused window, so your lane keys can be sampled while you type elsewhere during a map. A tap shorter than the polling interval may be missed. Windows only for now.
settings.keys.enabled_hint: Feeds the lane keys overlay with presses and keys per second. A change needs a restart.
settings.keys.status.unsupported: Not supported on this system. Lane keys work on Windows only for now.
settings.keys.status.unknown: Could not check whether this system is supported.
settings.keys.layout_help: Auto picks 4K or 7K from the map being played.
